title: PATOQ
text:
Start Here


1. Build foundations
Study biology, math, statistics, and computing fundamentals.
Open prerequisites


2. Learn the workflow
Follow one reproducible analysis pipeline from question to report.
Open core workflow


3. Go deep by topic
Choose omics, modeling, platforms, or specialized topics.
Open main sections




How to use this book effectively


Pick a weekly study plan and stick to one mini project at a time.

Keep your notes and scripts in GitHub from day one.

Use the Additional Resources chapter to deepen areas based on your goals.

title: Prerequisites
text:
How To Use This Book


Fast path (for lab members who need results quickly)


Study computer_science_fundamentals.qmd and core-bioinformatics-workflow.qmd first.

Start one small project with public data.

Return to biology/math/statistics chapters to strengthen weak areas.




Deep path (for undergrads building long-term foundations)


Complete the four foundations chapters in order.

After each chapter, do one mini project or reproducible notebook.

Move to omics-data.qmd, then modeling/integrated platforms.

title: Prerequisites
text:
Learning Philosophy

Learn broad fundamentals first, then build depth in one subfield.

Prefer reproducible work (version control, notebooks, clear notes).

Keep a personal glossary and question list while studying.

title: 4  Computer science fundamentals and resources
text:
4.5 Version Control: Git and GitHub

4.5.1 Why It Matters
Git helps you track changes, collaborate safely, and recover from mistakes without losing your work history.


4.5.2 Core Concepts

Repository: your tracked project folder
Commit: a saved checkpoint
Branch: an isolated line of work
Pull Request: proposed changes for review



4.5.3 Quick Command Workflow
# Clone project and create a feature branch
git clone https://github.com/username/repository.git
cd repository
git checkout -b feature/your-topic

# Work, commit, and push
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Add your update"
git pull --rebase
git push -u origin feature/your-topic


4.5.4 Beginner-Safe Recovery Patterns
# Unstage a file (keep edits)
git restore --staged path/to/file

# Discard local edits in one file
git restore path/to/file

# Revert a bad commit with a new safe commit
git revert <commit_hash>

# Temporarily save unfinished work
git stash push -m "wip: notes"
git stash pop
Avoid destructive commands (for example git reset --hard) unless you fully understand the impact.

title: 5  Core Bioinformatics Workflow
text: 5.1 Learning Outcomes

title: 5  Core Bioinformatics Workflow
text:
Move from raw data to interpretable biological results.
Keep analyses reproducible and version-controlled.
Report methods and decisions clearly.

title: 5  Core Bioinformatics Workflow
text:
5.2 The Workflow

Define the biological question and study design.
Collect data and metadata (with clear sample labels).
Perform quality control and basic exploratory analysis.
Run the core analysis (alignment/quantification/modeling).
Validate findings with controls or external evidence.
Visualize, interpret, and report results reproducibly.

title: 5  Core Bioinformatics Workflow
text:
5.3 Minimal Reproducibility Checklist

Keep all scripts/notebooks in Git.
Pin software versions when possible.
Separate raw data, intermediate files, and final results.
Track parameters and random seeds.
Document assumptions and limitations.

title: 5  Core Bioinformatics Workflow
text:
5.4 Suggested Project Skeleton
project/
  data/
    raw/
    processed/
  notebooks/
  scripts/
  results/
  figures/
  README.md

title: 5  Core Bioinformatics Workflow
text:
5.5 Starter Mini Project


Example: Differential expression quick practice


Pick a public dataset (e.g., GEO or SRA-derived matrix).

Define two biological groups and one contrast.

Run QC + normalization + differential testing.

Report top genes/pathways with one figure and one table.

10.5 Courses

Foundations Of Computational And Systems Biology

MIT OCW / This course is an introduction to computational biology emphasizing the fundamentals of nucleic acid and protein sequence and structural analysis; it also includes an introduction to the analysis of complex biological systems. Topics covered in the course include principles and methods used for sequence alignment, motif finding, structural modeling, structure prediction and network modeling, as well as currently emerging research areas. 7.91J | Spring 2014 | Graduate

10.6 Books

10.6.0.1 Learn R programming for FREE:

Hands-On Programming with R

This is the website for “Hands-On Programming with R”. This book will teach you how to program in R, with hands-on examples. He wrote it for non-programmers to provide a friendly introduction to the R language.

R for Data Science (1e)

This is the website for the first edition of “R for Data Science”, published January 2017.

R for Data Science (2e)

This is the website for the work-in-progress 2nd edition of “R for Data Science”. This book will teach you how to do data science with R: You’ll learn how to get your data into R, get it into the most useful structure, transform it and visualize.

Advanced R (1e)

This is the companion website for “Advanced R”, a book in Chapman & Hall’s R Series. The book is designed primarily for R users who want to improve their programming skills and understanding of the language.

Advanced R (2e)

This is the website for 2nd edition of “Advanced R”, a book in Chapman & Hall’s R Series. The book is designed primarily for R users who want to improve their programming skills and understanding of the language.

ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis (3e)

This is the on-line version of work-in-progress 3rd edition of “ggplot2: elegant graphics for data analysis” published by Springer.

R Cookbook, 2nd Edition

This book is full of how-to recipes, each of which solves a specific problem. The recipe includes a quick introduction to the solution followed by a discussion that aims to unpack the solution and give you some insight into how it works. We know these recipes are useful and we know they work, because we use them ourselves.

Text Mining with R: A Tidy Approach

This book serves as an introduction of text mining using the tidytext package and other tidy tools in R. The functions provided by the tidytext package are relatively simple; what is important are the possible applications. Thus, this book provides compelling examples of real text mining problems.
